reason: Both answers give the right verdict (very worried) and cover remote selector config, canary tests, owned-user capture, channel diversification and a ToS audit. Neither contains a misleading error. B adds specifics that would change what the asker does next: a sidePanel fallback so the workflow survives a DOM break, email capture on onInstalled before the user touches YouTube, narrow host permissions to avoid slow manual CWS review, and a tighter channel-concentration target. A's extras (cross-browser port, ytInitialData) are weaker or only partly relevant, and its "fail silently" leaves users with nothing. B is slightly stronger.
